Lab 4 · Weather Stations Monitoring — Bonus

Cloud Deployment Report

Two AWS EC2 free-tier VMs, a managed Aiven PostgreSQL database, and everything that broke — and got fixed — along the way.

10/10 stations running central-station healthy Kafka + Zookeeper healthy Aiven Postgres connected

This session took the Weather Stations Monitoring system — already implemented and tested locally with Docker Compose and Kubernetes manifests — and deployed it as the assignment's cloud bonus: the ten weather stations and the Kafka/central-station stack split across two separate AWS virtual machines, writing into a PostgreSQL database managed by Aiven rather than a self-hosted one. Everything below reflects the system as it stood at the end of the session, with real data pulled live from the deployment.

01

Architecture

Same application code as the Kubernetes deliverable — the only thing that changes for the bonus is where each piece runs.

Full technical detail on this split (listener configuration, security groups, compose files) lives in cloud/README.md in the repository.

02

Deployment log

What was actually clicked and run, in order.

Provisioned two EC2 instances

us-east-1 (N. Virginia) · Ubuntu Server 22.04 LTS · t3.micro · same VPC + subnet

weather-stations-vm and central-station-vm, one shared key pair, placed in the same subnet so they can reach each other over private IPs without exposing anything extra to the internet.

Locked down security groups

SSH (22) restricted to my IP on both. Kafka (9092) on central-station-vm opened only to weather-stations-sg — not 0.0.0.0/0 — so the broker is reachable by the other VM and nothing else.

Created the Aiven PostgreSQL service

Free tier, SSL enforced by default. Connection details (host, port, database, user, password) captured and injected only as environment variables on the VM — never committed to the repo.

Bootstrapped Docker on both VMs

Installed Docker CE + the Compose plugin via cloud/bootstrap.sh, cloned the repository onto each machine.

Brought up the central stack, then the stations

docker compose -f docker-compose.central.yml up -d --build on the central VM, then the equivalent for the ten stations once Kafka was confirmed healthy.

Verified end to end

Watched readings land in Aiven, rain alerts appear on the Kafka topic, and per-station counts settle into a stable, balanced pattern.

03

What went wrong, and the fix

Free-tier VMs have 1 GB of RAM. Default JVM heap sizing does not know that.

Incident

Kafka crash-looping on central-station-vm

Symptom
Kafka container stuck restarting; docker compose ps showed Restarting (1) in a loop.
Cause
Bitnami's Kafka image defaults to a 1 GB JVM heap — that alone exceeds the VM's entire 908 MB of RAM, before Zookeeper or central-station even start.
Fix
KAFKA_HEAP_OPTS=-Xmx350m, ZOO_HEAP_SIZE=160, JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS=-Xmx224m for central-station, plus a 512 MB swap file for headroom.
Incident

Disk full on the same VM

Symptom
fallocate: No space left on device — the 8 GB default root volume was completely full.
Cause
Docker images, Maven build cache, and (ironically) the swap file added moments earlier all competed for the same 8 GB disk.
Fix
Pruned the Docker build cache, cleaned apt's cache, and right-sized the swap file to 512 MB instead of the 2 GB first attempted.
Incident

Weather-stations VM thrashing

Symptom
Load average of 44 on a 2-vCPU box; 27 MB RAM free; SSH sessions barely responding.
Cause
Ten separate JVMs, each defaulting to roughly a quarter of host RAM (~227 MB) with no cap set — ten stations tried to claim ~2.3 GB combined on a 908 MB machine.
Fix
JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS=-Xmx48m per station — plenty for an app sending one small JSON message a second — plus a 1 GB swap file as a safety margin. Load dropped from 44 to under 6 within a minute of recreating the containers.

All three fixes are committed to cloud/docker-compose.central.yml and cloud/docker-compose.stations.yml on main, so the deployment reproduces cleanly for anyone following the same steps.
